name: Amartya Sen
role: Indian economist and philosopher, Nobel laureate in economics (1998)
summary: Sen, Nobel-winning economist, defends democracy as a universal value, rejects the 'Asian values' thesis and argues for a pragmatic mix of markets, public services and regulation that pays special attention to the poor.

sources.title: Democracy as a Universal Value, Journal of Democracy 10(3), July 1999
sources.author: Amartya Sen
sources.usedFor: Democracy as a universal value, the Indian experience, 'Asian values', the Lee hypothesis and what democracy requires.

sources.title: Capitalism Beyond the Crisis, The New York Review of Books, 26 March 2009 (reprint on Countercurrents)
sources.author: Amartya Sen
sources.usedFor: Markets, public services, regulation and the poor after the 2008 financial crisis, read through Adam Smith and Pigou.

sources.title: Amartya Sen, Biographical (Nobel Prize autobiography, 1998), NobelPrize.org
sources.author: Amartya Sen
sources.usedFor: The Bengal famine, Tagore and communal identities, the 1940s killings.

notes: First audit of a living writer, from three texts by him: his Nobel autobiography (1998) and two full-text essays: 'Democracy as a Universal Value' (1999) and 'Capitalism Beyond the Crisis' (NYRB, 2009, a reprint).
